faqs.question: What license does a fintech company need?
faqs.answer: Depending on the model, fintech businesses may need MSB, EMI, payment institution, or related AML/KYC and data protection registrations.

faqs.question: How do I form an AI company in the United States?
faqs.answer: Typical steps include choosing entity type and state, structuring IP ownership, obtaining an EIN, setting up banking, and preparing founder or developer agreements.

faqs.question: Can a crypto company operate in Singapore?
faqs.answer: It may be possible, but the token model, custody, exchange activity, AML obligations, and licensing requirements should be assessed before launch.

faqs.question: What should cross-border e-commerce businesses watch for?
faqs.answer: Key issues include entity structure, payment gateways, VAT/GST, sales terms, return policies, consumer protection, and logistics.

items.title: US SaaS Startup → Singapore Holding Structure
items.context: A US-based SaaS company with global customers needed a tax-efficient holding structure to manage IP, receive foreign revenue, and facilitate future fundraising.
items.solution: SOLEON established a Singapore private limited company as the IP holding entity, with a US subsidiary for operations. We handled ACRA registration, nominee director, and DBS business account opening.
items.result: Reduced effective tax rate on IP income from 21% to 17%. Company closed its Series A round within 6 months of restructuring.

items.title: Vietnam Manufacturer → Hong Kong Expansion
items.context: A Vietnamese manufacturing group needed a Hong Kong entity to facilitate international trade invoicing, improve banking access, and attract foreign distribution partners.
items.solution: SOLEON incorporated a Hong Kong limited company, set up with major international banks, and drafted distributor agreements compliant with both HK and international law.
items.result: Client secured 3 new European distribution contracts within 4 months. Banking setup completed in 2 weeks.

items.title: Fintech Startup → UAE Freezone Setup
items.context: A UK-based fintech startup needed a Middle East presence with proper payment licensing to serve GCC clients without the regulatory burden of mainland UAE.
items.solution: SOLEON advised on DIFC vs ADGM structure, completed DIFC freezone incorporation, and coordinated with local counsel on DFSA financial services licensing.
items.result: Licensed and operational in 8 weeks. Client onboarded first GCC enterprise client within 3 months.
